Flavoring.fact: A flavoring (or flavouring), also called flavor (or flavour) or flavorant, is a food additive that is used to improve the taste or smell of food. A flavoring is defined as a substance that gives another substance taste, altering the characteristics of the solute, causing it to become sweet, sour, tangy, etc.

Flavoring.subject: Applied Sciences
Flavoring.question: Also flavor enhancers are not considered flavorings under the EU legislation but additives (Point 14 of Annex I of Regulation (EC) No _____/2008)
Flavoring.fact: Also flavor enhancers are not considered flavorings under the EU legislation but additives (Point 14 of Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008).

Flight control surfaces.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight control surfaces.question: The _____ was Surface that allows a pilot to adjust and control an aircraft's flight attitude.
Flight control surfaces.fact: Flight control surfaces are aerodynamic devices allowing a pilot to adjust and control the aircraft's flight attitude. Flight control surfaces are generally operated by dedicated aircraft flight control systems.

Flight control surfaces.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight control surfaces.question: In an attempt to circumvent the Wrights' patent, _____ developed hinged movable surfaces called ailerons, attached to the wings, which helped controlling the roll of the aircraft
Flight control surfaces.fact: In an attempt to circumvent the Wrights' patent, Glenn Curtiss developed hinged movable surfaces called ailerons, attached to the wings, which helped controlling the roll of the aircraft.

Flight control surfaces.fact: as on the Fieseler Fi 156 Storch) give excellent slow speed and STOL capabilities, but compromise higher speed performance.

Flip-disc display.subject: Applied Sciences
Flip-disc display.question: The _____ was Electromechanical equivalent.
Flip-disc display.fact: The flip-disc display (or flip-dot display) is an electromechanical dot matrix display technology used for large outdoor signs, normally those that will be exposed to direct sunlight. A few game shows have also used flip-disc displays, including Canadian shows like Just Like Mom, The Joke's on Us and Uh Oh!, but most notably the American game show Family Feud from 1976 to 1995, and its British version Family Fortunes from 1980 to 2002.

Flip-disc display.subject: Applied Sciences
Flip-disc display.question: Flip-disc technology has been used for external destination signs on buses and trains across _____, Europe, Australia and Asia, as well as for variable-message signs on highways
Flip-disc display.fact: Flip-disc technology has been used for external destination signs on buses and trains across North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, as well as for variable-message signs on highways.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: The _____ was Exhaust for a fireplace, furnace etc.
Flue.fact: A flue is a pipe, or opening in a chimney for conveying exhaust gases from a fireplace, furnace, water heater, boiler, or generator to the outdoors. Historically the term flue meant the chimney itself.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: In the _____, they are also known as vents for boilers and as breeching for water heaters and modern furnaces
Flue.fact: In the United States, they are also called vents for boilers and as breeching for water heaters and modern furnaces.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Vent connectors join the appliance outlet to the vent or chimney; they are part of the venting system and are distinct from _____ ductwork
Flue.fact: Vent connectors join the appliance outlet to the vent or chimney; they are part of the venting system and are distinct from HVAC ductwork.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: The fuel gas code provides prescriptive sizing for natural-draft venting systems serving one or more listed appliances (including draft-hood and fan-assisted _____ I units listed for Type B vent)
Flue.fact: The fuel gas code provides prescriptive sizing for natural-draft venting systems serving one or more listed appliances (including draft-hood and fan-assisted Category I units listed for Type B vent).

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Mixing components from different vent manufacturers is not permitted in UL-_____ systems
Flue.fact: Where plastic piping is used, the appliance must be listed for that venting material; plastic vent systems either follow the appliance-specified product standards or are listed and labeled to UL 1738 (USA) and installed per the vent manufacturer’s instructions (including requirements such as contrasting-color primer where applicable). Mixing components from different vent manufacturers is not permitted in UL-1738 systems.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Observe maximum horizontal lengths and required clearances to combustibles per code and listing (e.g., single-wall connector max length typically _____ of chimney/vent height, unless engineered)
Flue.fact: Observe maximum horizontal lengths and required clearances to combustibles per code and listing (e.g., single-wall connector max length typically 75% of chimney/vent height, unless engineered).

Formal science.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal science.question: The _____ was Study of abstract structures described by formal systems.
Formal science.fact: Formal science is a branch of science studying disciplines concerned with abstract structures described by formal systems. Whereas the natural sciences and social sciences seek to characterize physical systems and social systems, respectively, using theoretical and empirical methods, the formal sciences use language tools concerned with characterizing abstract structures described by formal systems and the deductions that can be made from them.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: The _____ was Basic framework of mathematics.
Foundations of mathematics.fact: Foundations of mathematics are the logical and mathematical frameworks that allow the development of mathematics without generating self-contradictory theories, and to have reliable concepts of theorems, proofs, algorithms, etc. The term "foundations of mathematics" was not coined before the end of the 19th century, although foundations were first set up by the ancient Greek philosophers under the name of Aristotle's logic and systematically applied in Euclid's Elements.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: These foundations were tacitly assumed to be definitive until the introduction of infinitesimal calculus by Isaac Newton and _____ in the 17th century
Foundations of mathematics.fact: These foundations were tacitly assumed to be definitive until the introduction of infinitesimal calculus by Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz in the 17th century.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: This framework is based on a systematic use of axiomatic method and on set theory, specifically _____–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice
Foundations of mathematics.fact: This framework is based on a systematic use of axiomatic method and on set theory, specifically Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: It seems that ancient _____ philosophers were the first to study the nature of mathematics and its relation with the real world
Foundations of mathematics.fact: It seems that ancient Greek philosophers were the first to study the nature of mathematics and its relation with the real world.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences

Foundations of mathematics.fact: His method anticipated that of Dedekind cuts in the modern definition of real numbers by Richard Dedekind (1831–1916); see Eudoxus of Cnidus § Eudoxus' proportions.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: In the _____, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In the Posterior Analytics, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems.

Foundations of mathematics.question: So, for _____, a proved theorem is true, while in the axiomatic methods, the proof says only that the axioms imply the statement of the theorem
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In the Posterior Analytics, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems. Aristotle took a majority of his examples for this from arithmetic and from geometry, and his logic served as the foundation of mathematics for centuries.
